title: The day between
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Wednesday, the day between the job's days. Wood at the college with the smell of mat board on him. The instructor asks what changed. He says his hands. She says she meant the essay. He hasn't written one. She meant his hands.

panels.composition: The classroom. WOOD at the back, his hands on the desk, a paper cut on one thumb. The INSTRUCTOR passing.

image.prompt: a young man at the back of a classroom with his hands flat on the desk and a paper cut on one thumb, an instructor passing his row, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The hands: a cut, a bevel of dried glue, a smear of graphite from marking mat.

image.prompt: close on a young man's hands with a paper cut, dried glue and pencil smudges, black and white, no words
a woman instructor looking down at a student's hands, dry, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood drawing his own hands on the pad. The first time. They come out older than he is.

image.prompt: close on a drawing pad with an ink drawing of a pair of hands that look older than the young man drawing them, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: His hands, drawn for the first time. Older than he is.
